what_happened: The operator wrote a request for the replay gate on new refusal rules (job 20261028-154034-kncc). It exempted a rule from the gate "unless the criteria say a higher refusal rate is intended". The gate checked for that phrase, not for a measured number. A rule that would have refused about 80% of past accepted readings then landed, because its criteria contained the phrase. The operator logged this as a mistake.
cause: Requests and gates are allowed to define exceptions as wording, and nothing requires an exception to carry a measurable limit. A text match is satisfied by anyone who writes the phrase, so the gate cannot tell a justified exception from a bad rule. No review step asks of a new gate what the largest effect is that an exception could let through.
prevention: Make the replay gate compare the measured refusal rate on past accepted readings against a fixed ceiling in code, such as a percentage set in athena.toml. A phrase in the criteria must not lift that ceiling. If a higher rate is really intended, the exemption must state a numeric bound, and the gate must check the measured rate against that bound. Any rate above the ceiling with no bound, or above the stated bound, holds the job for the owner. Also add a rule to request review: an exemption written as words with no number is rejected.
proposed_request: Change the refusal-rule replay gate so it enforces a numeric limit and not a phrase. Outcome: when a new or changed reading-refusal rule is replayed against past accepted readings, the job is held if the measured refusal rate is above a ceiling set in athena.toml (default 5%). Stating in the criteria that a higher refusal rate is intended must not lift the ceiling. A job may raise the limit only by stating an explicit numeric bound in its criteria (for example, "refusal rate up to 15%"), and the gate then checks the measured rate against that bound. Acceptance: (1) a test with a rule that refuses 80% of a fixture of past readings is held even when the criteria contain the old phrase "a higher refusal rate is intended"; (2) a rule at 3% passes with no declaration; (3) a rule at 12% with a stated bound of 15% passes, and at 20% with the same bound is held; (4) the held message names the measured rate and the limit. Remove the phrase-matching exemption. Use the existing replay data and do not change other admission rules.
